# IRONICS Client Distribution — D2 Scope (PROPOSAL)

**Status:** PROPOSED 2026-09-06 — nothing here is implemented, deployed or provisioned. Operator approval required per tier.  
**Origin:** operator mandate after the 0.1.2 download incident — *"institutional grade AAA solution … users should be able to download fairly quickly."*  
**Method:** 5 research lenses (CDN/edge + cost, AAA client mechanics, existing platform constraints, integrity/abuse, package-size levers) → architect synthesis → adversarial staff-level review. Review verdict: **sound-with-fixes**.  
**Scope boundary:** the tester's *empty* 0.1.2 zip was a packaging defect (bsdtar `./` entries; fixed in 0.1.2.1). This document addresses the separate, latent delivery defects it exposed, and the longer-term path.

## Executive summary

The incident is a design bug, not a slow origin: GET /v1/download/latest mints an S3 presigned URL with a 900 s TTL, signed with the Lambda's own execution-role credentials (latest.ts:14, :42, :71-75); S3 re-checks that signature on every request, so any browser resume/Range GET issued after minute 15 gets 403 and the file is left truncated -- and simply raising the TTL cannot fix it, because AWS states a role-signed presigned URL also dies when the role session expires (~1 h) regardless of expiresIn. RECOMMENDATION: implement the plan of record that the shipped D1 deliberately deviated from (BPD s11 / D1 plan s3): CloudFront + Origin Access Control in front of the existing private ironics-releases bucket, with a 24-hour CloudFront-signed URL minted by the same APPROVED-gated Lambda. Tier 0 ships that same-day on the default *.cloudfront.net host (no certificate or DNS wait) plus no-regret publish hardening (sidecars, headers, verify one-liner); Tier 1 (days) adds dl.ironics.org, per-download telemetry (standard logs -> Athena), a per-account mint quota, the CloudFront Pro flat-rate plan ($15/mo, 50 TB), and a config-only package cull from 3.9 GB to ~3.0 GB; Tier 2 (weeks) delivers an IRONICS launcher with parallel chunked Range downloads, verify/repair, and delta patches so weekly updates shrink from 3.9 GB to an estimated 100-500 MB, plus per-venue chunking so a fresh install is ~1.05-1.8 GB. VERDICT CloudFront over Cloudflare R2: at the 7-8 TB/month a 500-tester beta generates, CloudFront Pro is $15/mo flat vs R2 about $5/mo; that $10 buys edge caching of the whole 3.9 GB object (CloudFront caches up to 50 GB per object; Cloudflare's cache cap is 512 MB on every non-Enterprise plan), one provenance-gated copy of each release instead of a dual-publish, one vendor in the byte path, and a built-in signer -- R2 remains the documented cost lever, triggered only if sustained egress exceeds 50 TB/month after Tier 2 has shrunk patches. COST: $0 egress today under CloudFront's always-free 1 TB/month (or $15/mo on Pro), ~$0.40/mo for one new secret, no new vendors. WHEN TESTERS SEE IT: the moment Tier 0 deploys, a 3.9 GB download on 50 Mbps still takes ~11-13 min and on 10 Mbps ~55-60 min (link-bound -- no CDN beats the line rate), but every pause, Wi-Fi drop or browser restart inside 24 h resumes instead of failing; Tier 1B cuts those to ~9 / ~44 min; Tier 2 makes a weekly patch ~1 min / ~4 min and a fresh install ~3-5 min / ~14-24 min. Everything in this document is a PROPOSAL requiring operator approval -- nothing has been implemented, deployed or provisioned.

## Root cause of the delivery-class defect

Three stacked facts, all verified in code and AWS documentation. (1) C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\src\handlers\download\latest.ts:14 sets URL_TTL_SECONDS = 900 and :71-75 mints an S3 presigned GET; the comment at :12-13 asserts this is "not a total-download deadline", which is true ONLY for an unbroken TCP stream. AWS: "if the connection drops and the client tries to restart the download after the expiration time passes, the download fails." A Wi-Fi hiccup, a laptop sleep, or Chrome's own resume (a new Range + If-Range request) after minute 15 therefore receives 403; Chrome marks the download Failed/Interrupted and the .zip is left truncated -- "came through empty". (2) The URL is signed with `new S3Client({})` (latest.ts:42) = the Lambda execution role's temporary credentials. AWS: "IAM role credentials -- The presigned URL expires when the role session expires, even if you specify a longer expiration time" (STS AssumeRole default 1 h). So the obvious hotfix -- raise URL_TTL_SECONDS to 24 h -- is silently capped at roughly one hour and would have failed this same tester (>1 h download). The only S3-direct escape is a long-lived IAM user access key (7-day SigV4 max), which AWS-SETUP.md:6 forbids in spirit ("never put a long-lived access key") and which would be thrown away by the CDN tier; rejected. (3) Delivery is a single browser connection straight to S3 in Virginia with no edge, no per-request logging, and no verify step: DownloadCard.tsx:64 does `window.location.href = url`; the bucket has no server-access logs (ironics-portal-stack.ts:307-314); the only telemetry is `download_started` (latest.ts:78) -- so nobody could see the 403s or the tester's actual throughput. The two earlier builds "worked" because those testers finished inside 15 minutes: 3,906,129,510 bytes = 31.25 Gbit needs >= ~35 Mbps sustained to finish in 15 min; the measured 117 Mbps single-stream from the dev machine proves the ORIGIN is fast and that the failure is TTL x slow link x single connection x no resume authorization. The fix is therefore a signer whose validity is not bound to any credential session (CloudFront key group) with a validity window >= 6x the worst plausible download, native Range/206 at the edge, and a size/sha256 check the tester can run.

## Tiers

### Tier 0 -- same day (4-8 h): kill the incident class on the existing AWS stack, nothing throwaway

**What it buys:** Download time is link-bound and UNCHANGED in the ideal case: 3,906,129,510 B = 31.25 Gbit -> 50 Mbps: 10.4 min ideal / ~11-13 min realistic (single stream, Wi-Fi); 10 Mbps: 52 min ideal / ~55-60 min realistic. What changes: every resume, Range GET, pause, sleep or browser restart inside 24 h is authorized and served as 206 from the nearest of 750+ edges (edge TCP termination also raises single-stream throughput on long-RTT/lossy links), so the 'empty file' failure mode is gone; the tester can prove completeness in seconds (size) and integrity in ~1 min (sha256). Weekly patch = still the full 3.9 GB zip.

**Cost (monthly):** Egress $0 up to CloudFront's always-free 1 TB/month (~256 full downloads of 3.9 GB), then $0.085/GB US/EU (= $0.33 per download); S3->CloudFront origin fetch $0; Secrets Manager $0.40/mo; distribution/OAC/key group $0 at rest. Current beta (~10 testers x 4 downloads = 156 GB): $0.40/mo total vs ~$5/mo on S3-direct today.  
**Effort:** 4-8 engineer-hours: ~120 LOC CDK, ~30 LOC handler, 2 test edits, 1 dependency (@aws-sdk/cloudfront-signer), ~25 LOC publish script, card copy; `cdk diff` + changeset Replacement probe (house rule -- expect an ADD of the distribution/key/secret and an UPDATE of the bucket policy, NO bucket replacement since bucketName is unchanged), deploy via the existing deploy-api.yml OIDC pipeline or local; operator steps: generate key pair, put-secret-value, one watched throttled pause/resume test. Distribution creation propagates in ~5-15 min.  
**Risk:** LOW. A 24 h bearer URL is shareable for 24 h (mitigations: acct/rid attribution in the URL, key-group kill switch, Tier 1 mint quota; no IP binding because CloudFront custom-policy IpAddress is IPv4-only and breaks CGNAT/VPN/mobile). First fetch of each new version per edge is a Virginia origin miss (no worse than today). CloudFront caches ranges per Range request so a partially cached object serves the cached ranges and fetches the rest -- benign. Signed-URL vs signed-cookie: URL is correct here because cookies cannot be scoped to *.cloudfront.net from ironics.org and a URL survives browser restarts and works with download managers; cookies arrive in Tier 2 for multi-chunk delivery once dl.ironics.org exists.

**Scope:**

- 0.1 CloudFront distribution in IronicsPortalStack: origin = existing private `ironics-releases` bucket via Origin Access Control (CDK `S3BucketOrigin.withOriginAccessControl` writes the bucket-policy statement allowing only principal cloudfront.amazonaws.com with AWS:SourceArn = this distribution; Block-Public-Access stays ON); GET/HEAD only, HTTPS only, HTTP/2+3, managed CachingOptimized cache policy (no cookies/headers/query in the cache key), compression OFF (zip is outside the 1,000-10,000,000-byte compress range anyway and compression would break 206), cookie logging OFF, IPv6 on, Origin Shield off, price class ALL (or 100 if testers are NA/EU only). Use the DEFAULT `dXXXX.cloudfront.net` hostname so no ACM certificate or Cloudflare DNS step is on the critical path -- the custom domain is added in Tier 1 without changing anything built here.
- 0.2 Key group: generate an RSA-2048 key pair (openssl), commit the PUBLIC PEM as a `cloudfront.PublicKey` + `KeyGroup`, create a new empty `sm.Secret` `ironics/portal/cf-signing-key` (RETAIN, populated out-of-band with put-secret-value -- the exact discipline of the three existing secrets at ironics-portal-stack.ts:277-294). Trusted key group required on the default behavior. Removing the public key from the key group is the emergency kill-switch for every outstanding link.
- 0.3 Handler: latest.ts replaces `getSignedUrl(s3, GetObjectCommand)` with `@aws-sdk/cloudfront-signer` `getSignedUrl({ url: https://<host>/<pointer.key>?acct=<sha256(accountId).slice(0,12)>&rid=<ulid>, keyPairId, privateKey, dateLessThan: now + 86400 s })`; returns expiresIn: 86400; the APPROVED/BANNED/SUSPENDED account-row check (:47-53), the BOM-safe latest.json read (:57-62) and the response contract {url, version, channel, file, sizeBytes, sha256, expiresIn} are byte-for-byte unchanged. Route spec api.ts:155-161 gains a `secrets:` arm (CF_SIGNING_SECRET_ID) + env CF_DOWNLOAD_HOST / CF_KEY_PAIR_ID, and `s.releases.grantRead(f)` is NARROWED to `win64/latest.json` (the Lambda no longer needs GetObject on the zip). Tests: download.test.ts:151 asserts `Signature=` and `Key-Pair-Id=` instead of `X-Amz-Signature`, :155 expects 86400; grants.test.ts:84 gains the secret arm.
- 0.4 Publish hardening in publish-release.ps1 (no infra needed, reused by every later tier): `aws s3 cp` with `--content-type application/zip --content-disposition "attachment; filename=IRONICS-<ver>-Win64.zip" --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" --checksum-algorithm SHA256`; upload `manifest.json` and `IRONICS-<ver>-Win64.sha256` beside the zip at win64/<ver>/ (they already exist at D:\BagMan\releases\win64\<ver>\ but are never uploaded today); after upload, head-object and assert ContentLength == local size before writing latest.json.
- 0.5 DownloadCard copy (no contract change): show exact byte count next to the GiB figure, 'This link works for 24 hours -- you can pause, lose Wi-Fi, or restart the browser and resume', an expected-minutes line (size / user-entered or default 50 Mbps), and a one-line Verify block: `Get-FileHash .\IRONICS-<ver>-Win64.zip -Algorithm SHA256` with the rule 'if the size is not exactly N bytes the download is incomplete -- resume it, do not unzip'.
- 0.6 Acceptance (doctrine: watched, not asserted): from a throttled client (`curl --limit-rate 1250k -o build.zip <url>` or a tethered link), start the download, kill it at minute 20, resume with `curl -C - ...` / Chrome Resume, observe HTTP 206 + Content-Range, let it finish, and confirm sha256 == latest.json. Also confirm a direct `https://ironics-releases.s3.amazonaws.com/win64/...` GET is still 403 (bucket private) and that a URL with dateLessThan in the past is 403 at CloudFront.

**Preserves:** APPROVED-only gate: the account-row check in latest.ts:47-53 is untouched; the URL is still minted only by the session-guarded route; Immutability: publish-release.ps1:60-61 head-object refusal unchanged; bucket versioned + RETAIN; immutable keys need no CloudFront invalidation; Provenance gate: publish-release.ps1:38-42 child-PowerShell verify_ship_provenance.ps1 exit-code gate unchanged (UE5-CL-0); sha256 manifest: latest.json unchanged; manifest.json + .sha256 sidecars now ALSO live beside the zip; No public URLs: bucket stays BLOCK_ALL; only the distribution principal can GetObject; CloudFront enforces signature + expiry on every request including Range; AWS + Cloudflare footprint only; client contract {url,...} unchanged so DownloadCard needs copy only; Least-privilege proof: the Lambda's S3 grant SHRINKS to latest.json; no IAM user, no long-lived access key

**Touches:** `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\lib\ironics-portal-stack.ts (+Distribution, OAC, PublicKey, KeyGroup, Secret `ironics/portal/cf-signing-key`; bucket policy statement on Releases)`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\lib\api.ts:155-161 (DownloadLatest route: secrets arm, env, narrowed releases grant)`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\src\handlers\download\latest.ts:7-14,42,71-75,87`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\package.json (+@aws-sdk/cloudfront-signer)`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\test\download.test.ts:151,155 ; test\grants.test.ts:84`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\scripts\publish-release.ps1:63-79 (headers, checksum, sidecars, post-upload size verify)`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\web\components\DownloadCard.tsx:26-33,109-125 (copy + verify block)`; `AWS acct 302659227808 us-east-1: 1 CloudFront distribution, 1 OAC, 1 public key, 1 key group, 1 Secrets Manager secret, 1 bucket-policy statement`

### Tier 1 -- days (1 week): institutional hardening, telemetry, cost plan, and a smaller package

**What it buys:** With 1B's ~3.0 GB (24 Gbit) package: 50 Mbps 8.0 min ideal / ~9 min realistic; 10 Mbps 40 min ideal / ~44 min realistic (vs 10.4/52 ideal today). Weekly patch = still the full ~3.0 GB zip. Plus: a branded, WAF-fronted download host; per-download speed/outcome/country data for cents; flat, predictable egress cost; documented rotation and kill-switch; ~650 MB of non-game bytes (MetaHuman/NNE/CEF3) that should never ship removed from every future patch.

**Cost (monthly):** CloudFront Pro $15/mo flat (or $0 PAYG under 1 TB) + log storage/Athena < $1/mo + Secrets Manager $0.40 + ACM $0. At 100 testers x 4 (1.56 TB): Pro $15 vs PAYG $48 vs S3-direct $131. At 500 x 4 (7.8 TB): Pro $15 vs PAYG $578 vs S3-direct $693. At 1,000 x 4 (15.6 TB): Pro $15 vs PAYG ~$1,213 vs S3-direct ~$1,395.  
**Effort:** 1A: 2-3 engineer-days (CDK alias + logging delivery + Athena table + quota + event + runbook) + 3 operator steps (ACM request/validation CNAME, dl CNAME, plan subscription). 1B: 1 operator-day of edits + one full Shipping cook on the 16 GB build PC (hours) + cooked lap + publish. Web card copy ships via local wrangler until the expired CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is renewed (CI web deploy is blocked on it).  
**Risk:** LOW-MEDIUM. ACM validation depends on the operator adding the CNAME (minutes to hours). Flat-rate plan: 'allowances are not hard limits' but sustained excess over 2-3 months may degrade edge placement -- irrelevant below 50 TB. 1B carries the doctrine risk that every NeverCook/plugin-scope change loses to a surviving hard reference: only a real cook + cooked boot proves it; the UDS/WebBrowserWidget runtime question is unverified; the 4K World cap is a visible (ARCANEON-only) change and the operator's 'don't re-tune proven' rule applies. None of 1A is throwaway for Tier 2; 1B's cuts persist in every later build.

**Scope:**

- 1A.1 dl.ironics.org: request an ACM certificate in us-east-1 (DNS-validated via a CNAME the operator adds at Cloudflare, exactly the out-of-band recipe used for api.ironics.org at api.ts:410-420), add `domainNames:["dl.ironics.org"]` + `certificate` to the Tier 0 distribution, and add ONE Cloudflare CNAME dl.ironics.org -> dXXXX.cloudfront.net set to DNS-ONLY (grey cloud). Never orange-cloud it: Cloudflare's proxy cannot cache >512 MB, would double-CDN, and its terms exclude serving large files through the plain CDN. CF_DOWNLOAD_HOST env flips; signing code unchanged.
- 1A.2 Telemetry: CloudFront standard logging v2 -> a new private log bucket (30-day lifecycle) in plain/JSON with Hive partitioning + an Athena partition-projection table; keep `?acct=&rid=` on the signed Resource (Tier 0) so `cs-uri-query` joins to a new server event `download_link_minted{rid, version}` (add to SERVER_EVENTS in events.ts:17-26 -- names are locked, so this is an addition, not a rename). A saved Athena view yields per-download bytes (sum sc-bytes vs sizeBytes), elapsed, effective Mbps (sc-bytes*8/time-taken), c-country, asn, and x-edge-detailed-result-type (ClientCommError = tester dropped). This is how the studio finally KNOWS tester speeds instead of assuming 50/10 Mbps. Cookie logging stays OFF so the ironics_session cookie (Domain=.ironics.org, sent to dl.ironics.org by the browser) never lands in logs.
- 1A.3 Anti-abuse: per-account mint quota (e.g. 20 mints/day) using the existing `IronicsRateLimits` DynamoDB pattern already granted at api.ts:140 -- NOTE AWS WAF cannot attach to an API Gateway v2 HTTP API, so the mint route is protected by the table, not WAF; a WAF web ACL with an IP rate-based rule goes on the CloudFront distribution instead (included on the flat-rate plan; PAYG ~$5/ACL + $1/rule + $0.60/M req). Key-rotation runbook (add new key -> switch signer -> remove old; 5 keys/group) and the kill switch documented in AWS-SETUP.md.
- 1A.4 Cost plan: subscribe the distribution to the CloudFront Pro flat-rate plan ($15/mo: 50 TB data transfer, 10M requests, WAF 25 rules, access logs, 50 GB S3 storage credit, DDoS; Signed URLs + OAC included) via console or the PricingPlanManager API (API support announced 2026-09; CloudFormation support unverified -- see decisions). Pro's 50 TB covers ~12,800 full 3.9 GB downloads/month; the per-distribution 150 Gbps quota does not apply on flat-rate plans. Alternatively stay PAYG while under ~256 downloads/month (free) and flip to Pro at the first month that would exceed 1 TB.
- 1A.5 Doc hygiene: fix the stale 'MANDATORY before any R2 upload' wording in C:\Dev\Bag_Man\Tools\verify_ship_provenance.ps1:7,89 and Docs\ENGINE_DOCTRINE.md:47-49 to 'release upload' (R2 was never provisioned); update Docs\IRONICS_D1_DISTRIBUTION_PLAN.md status and BPD s11 to record CloudFront as LIVE.
- 1B Package cull (Bag_Man repo, config + one asset, separate approval, runs in parallel with 1A): (i) restrict AgentIntegrationKit to the Editor target in Bag_Man.uproject:383-385 (its uplugin declares MetaHumanCharacter + MetaHumanSDK as optional deps at AgentIntegrationKit.uplugin:431-439, which is what drags 323 MB of face-tracker neural nets into the Game cook); (ii) disable NNEDenoiser (103 MB OIDN models cooked via its own +DirectoriesToAlwaysCook); (iii) make UltimateDifficultyScaling editor-only or drop its WebBrowserWidget dependency so 221 MB of CEF3 leaves Engine/Binaries -- AFTER confirming UDS has no runtime web-widget use; (iv) remove `+VulkanTargetedShaderFormats=SF_VULKAN_SM6` at Config\DefaultEngine.ini:339 (~-90 MB of shader code on a Windows-only beta); (v) HDRI_6 (AFLHub MegaBase, 268 MB loose / 116 MB on disk, TC_HDR uncompressed 8K) -> TC_HDR_Compressed + MaxTextureSize 4096 (~-100 MB); (vi) add a [Windows DeviceProfile] TextureLODGroups MaxLODSize=4096 for World/WorldNormalMap/WorldSpecular (cook-time mip strip, ~-155 MB, visible only on ARCANEON's DeepWaterStation UDIMs). Re-cook Shipping, diff the cook manifest, run the cooked 2-client lap, publish as 0.1.3 through the unchanged provenance gate. Expected ~-0.9 GB -> ~3.0 GB.
- 1A.6 Acceptance: repeat the Tier 0 throttled pause/resume test against dl.ironics.org; run the Athena view and see the test download's bytes/elapsed/outcome; confirm a revoked key (removed from the key group) 403s an outstanding URL within minutes.

**Preserves:** Everything Tier 0 preserves (gate, immutability, provenance, sha256, no public URLs, footprint, contract); The 'account row is truth' rule: the mint quota is added beside, not instead of, the status check; Cook doctrine: 1B lands only after cook manifest diff + cooked 2-client lap; no matchmaking/experience/EOS/GameLift surfaces touched; Bag_Man release ledger shape (releases/README.md): new version 0.1.3 is a new immutable key

### Tier 2 -- weeks (3-6 weeks): IRONICS launcher with chunked parallel downloads, verify/repair, delta patches, and per-venue chunks

**What it buys:** Fresh install: base-only 1.05 GB (8.4 Gbit) = 2.8 min @ 50 Mbps / 14 min @ 10 Mbps; base + hub bundled 1.8 GB (14.4 Gbit) = 4.8 min / 24 min; each venue on first visit 0.06-0.8 GB = 0.2-2 min @ 50 / 1-11 min @ 10. Full 3.9 GB via launcher: still ~10.4 / ~52 min ideal (parallel Range GETs cannot beat line rate but do beat single-stream Wi-Fi loss: Mathis bound MSS/(RTT*sqrt(p)) caps ONE stream near 2 Mbps at 60 ms RTT / 1% loss; 8-16 streams multiply that up to the line). WEEKLY PATCH: estimated 100-500 MB (MUST be measured in 2A); at 300 MB (2.4 Gbit) = ~48 s @ 50 Mbps / ~4 min @ 10 Mbps instead of 10.4 / 52 min. Verify/repair means a bad download costs one chunk, not 3.9 GB. Egress falls by roughly an order of magnitude, which keeps even 5,000 testers inside CloudFront Pro's 50 TB.

**Cost (monthly):** Infra unchanged (CloudFront Pro $15/mo); storage grows by one chunk store (~4-8 GB/version, within Pro's 50 GB S3 credit for 4-5 hot versions). Engineering: 2A 1-2 days; launcher MVP 2-3 weeks (Tauri) or 3-4 weeks (BPS/Slate); production polish 4-6 weeks; 2C ~1 week. No vendor fees (PatchKit/itch rejected: new vendor, their key gate is not the portal's APPROVED gate).  
**Effort:** 3-6 weeks of one engineer plus the operator-owned D: engine build lane for BuildPatchTool / a UE Program target and the cook for 2C. 2A must run first; 2B and 2C can proceed in parallel after it.  
**Risk:** MEDIUM. A second shipped product (auto-update, error taxonomy, SmartScreen). Real delta size unknown until 2A -- if IoStore ordering churns, Steam-style advice (1-2 GB packs, stable ordering) must be applied first. BPS is thinly documented; the Slate installer is heavy; Tauri needs Rust competence. 2C touches the protected travel/matchmaking flow and World Partition cook lottery (DefaultGame.ini:246-284 history). Nothing in Tiers 0-1 is discarded: same bucket, same distribution, same signer, same keys, same latest.json; the zip path stays as the fallback for browsers.

**Scope:**

- 2A Spike (1-2 days, decides the core): build `BuildPatchTool` from D:\UE5.6-source\Engine\Source\Programs\BuildPatchTool (only the editor DLL is prebuilt), run `-mode=PatchGeneration` on the staged 0.1.1 and 0.1.2 Shipping dirs (1 MiB rolling-hash chunks; only NEW chunks are written), then `-mode=DiffManifest` -> the REAL weekly delta size for this pak/ucas layout. This single number decides whether patches are ~100-500 MB or ~2 GB and whether IoStore container ordering must be stabilised. VERIFIED: BuildPatchServices has a clean auth injection point -- the installer's message handler answers `ChunkUriRequest` with `FChunkUriResponse{Uri, AdditionalHeaders}` (BuildPatchMessage.h:56-74), applied to every chunk GET at CloudChunkSource.cpp:735 / DownloadService.cpp:220 -- so a CloudFront signed cookie (or a per-chunk signed URL rewrite) can ride every request.
- 2B Launcher (decision after 2A): EITHER (i) a thin Tauri/Rust launcher (3-10 MB installer) with a fixed-1 MiB chunk manifest {sizeBytes, sha256, chunks[]} emitted by publish-release.ps1 and a Rust download core (reqwest + tokio + sha2, ~2k LOC), OR (ii) a UE Program/Slate installer linking BuildPatchServices (Epic Launcher internals: adaptive 1-100 parallel chunk downloads, retries, staged construction, ShaVerifyAllFiles, repair, delta policy; ~50-100 MB). Both: sign in with the portal session (cookie Domain=.ironics.org), call /v1/download/latest which now ALSO sets a CloudFront signed COOKIE (custom policy, Resource https://dl.ironics.org/win64/<ver>/*, 24 h -- this is why Tier 1's custom domain is mandatory), download 8-16 parallel Range GETs, re-mint on 401/403, chunk-bitmap resume, per-chunk + whole-file SHA verify, atomic staged swap, 'Verify / Repair' button, launch IRONICS.exe. Recommendation: (ii) if the 2A delta is small and the BPS Program target builds cleanly on D: -- zero bespoke download code and the same manifests later feed HTTPChunkInstaller (present in 5.6, EnabledByDefault false) for in-game streaming installs; otherwise (i).
- 2C Per-venue chunking (Bag_Man, ~1 week, parallel): chunking is already live (bGenerateChunks=true; ShooterCore emits pakchunk1 = 84.5 MB today). Author PrimaryAssetLabels (bLabelAssetsInMyDirectory) per venue root -> pakchunk10 AFLHub (~808 MB, ~700 after HDRI fix), 11 ShantyTown (574 MB, label its World Partition cells/DataLayers with the map), 12 ARCANEON closure DeepWaterStation+CyberPunk (323 MB, ~170 after 4K cap), 13 Officers Club (266 MB), 14 SkyClub (64 MB), 15 SpaceshipInterior (79 MB, verify it is referenced at all); shared assets fall to chunk 0. Base chunk measured from the container = ~977 MB + exe 206 MB + EOS 18 MB + movie 46 MB = ~1.25 GB today, ~1.05 GB after Tier 1B. Gate `AFLHubTravelComponent.cpp:46-48` ServerTravel on 'venue chunk mounted' with a progress UI (MOCKUP-FIRST: 1:1 mockup for operator approval before any engine build); bots/queue must never travel to an unmounted map. Every pakchunkN triplet is an immutable object beside the base at win64/<ver>/ and, being < 512 MB each, is also Cloudflare-edge-cacheable should Tier 3 ever trigger.
- 2D Publish tooling: publish-release.ps1 gains a `-Manifest` step (BPT PatchGeneration -CloudDir or the fixed-chunk manifest), uploads chunks/manifests under win64/<ver>/, keeps the zip for the browser path, and BPT `Compactify` prunes chunks no live version references. Provenance gate unchanged and still first.
- 2E Code signing decision: the launcher exe trips SmartScreen once without an Authenticode/EV cert (same as the game today). Decide before the launcher ships.
- 2F Acceptance: fresh install on a clean machine via the launcher; kill the machine mid-download and resume; corrupt one chunk on disk and watch Repair fetch only that chunk; apply a real weekly patch and read the transferred bytes from the Athena view; cooked 2-client lap through a venue that was mounted on demand.

**Preserves:** APPROVED gate: cookie/URL still minted only by the session-guarded, row-checking Lambda; the launcher never holds a credential, only a 24 h signed cookie; Immutability + provenance: chunks/manifests are new immutable keys behind the same provenance-gated publish script; BPT Compactify only deletes chunks no live manifest references; sha256: whole-file hash stays in latest.json/manifest.json; per-chunk hashes are additive; No public URLs: chunk behavior requires the trusted key group (signed cookie) exactly like the zip behavior; Lyra/UE-canonical: chunking via PrimaryAssetLabels + existing bGenerateChunks; no engine hacks; HTTPChunkInstaller/IoStore-OnDemand remain later options on the same layout; Mockup-first for the new download-at-door UI

**Touches:** `D:\UE5.6-source\Engine\Source\Programs\BuildPatchTool (build), Engine\Source\Runtime\Online\BuildPatchServices (ChunkUriRequest handler for auth headers)`; `New launcher repo (Tauri/Rust) OR a new UE Program target under Bag_Man Source/Programs`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\scripts\publish-release.ps1 (manifest/chunk publish, Compactify) ; src\handlers\download\latest.ts (+signed cookie for win64/<ver>/*) ; ironics-portal-stack.ts (second cache behavior for chunks)`; `C:\Dev\Bag_Man: PrimaryAssetLabel assets per venue root; Plugins\GameFeatures\AFLHub\Source\AFLHub\Private\AFLHubTravelComponent.cpp:46-48 ; Config\DefaultGame.ini:106 (bShouldAcquireMissingChunksOnLoad) ; new WBP for download progress (after mockup approval)`; `Docs: BUILD_PRUNE_DEPLOY_PLAN.md s6 Track D4 status; a launcher design doc; ledger records for chunked releases`

### Tier 3 -- CONDITIONAL cost lever (not scheduled): Cloudflare R2 delivery plane behind a gating Worker

**What it buys:** Same link-bound times as Tier 2 (fresh 1.05-1.8 GB: ~3-5 min @ 50 / ~14-24 min @ 10; weekly patch ~1 / ~4 min) with egress cost flat at any scale.

**Cost (monthly):** ~$5-6/mo (Workers Paid $5 + R2 storage ~$0.30 for ~30 GB after the 10 GB free tier; Class A/B ops within free tiers) vs CloudFront Premium $1,000-2,250/mo at 50-125 TB. Not worth it below 50 TB/month: vs Pro's $15 the saving is $10/mo against a second copy of every release, a second gate implementation, two vendors in the byte path, and no edge cache for the whole zip.  
**Effort:** 3-5 days (Worker + token mint + dual publish + AE dashboard + throughput measurement) when triggered.  
**Risk:** MEDIUM: second immutability surface (R2 has no CDK-managed versioning/RETAIN parity here), gate logic duplicated outside the audited apps/api grants model unless the Worker round-trips to the API, unmeasured per-object throughput, Cloudflare zone plan unknown (WAF token-auth needs Pro+).

**Scope:**

- Trigger BOTH of: (a) sustained CloudFront egress > 50 TB/month for 2+ months (i.e. beyond Pro/Business allowance, where the next step is Premium $1,000-2,250/mo) after Tier 2 delta patching is live; AND (b) a measured R2 single-stream throughput >= 100 Mbps to residential links from 2-3 geographies (undocumented today; S3 measured 117 Mbps).
- Shape if triggered: private R2 bucket `ironics-releases` (location hint ENAM), publish-release.ps1 dual-writes (aws s3 cp --endpoint-url r2 + head-object immutability check + size verify), one-shot Super Slurper/rclone backfill (~15 GB, ~$1.4 S3 egress once), a Worker `ironics-dl` on dl.ironics.org with an r2_buckets binding that validates a Lambda-minted 24 h HMAC token (path+acct+rid+exp, Worker secret) and streams `bucket.get(key,{range})` as 206 with ETag/Accept-Ranges/Content-Length, Analytics Engine data points for telemetry, Workers Paid ($5/mo). Tier 2's < 512 MB chunks are then edge-cacheable on the existing zone plan. S3 remains the provenance/RETAIN archive. R2 presigned URLs (no custom domain, bypass WAF) are the 1-day fallback shape but not the target.

**Preserves:** APPROVED gate stays in the Lambda (it mints the token); immutability + provenance via S3 archive + script checks; sha256 in latest.json (R2 ETags differ); no public bucket (no r2.dev); AWS + Cloudflare footprint only

**Touches:** `Cloudflare: R2 bucket, Worker ironics-dl + wrangler.jsonc (r2_buckets binding, route dl.ironics.org/*), Worker secret, Analytics Engine dataset`; `C:\Dev\Ironics-Platform\apps\api\scripts\publish-release.ps1 (dual-write) ; src\handlers\download\latest.ts (HMAC token) ; Secrets Manager (R2 keys + HMAC secret)`; `Cloudflare DNS: dl.ironics.org moves from grey-cloud CNAME to the Worker route`

## Recommendation

ONE PATH: CloudFront + OAC + long-lived CloudFront-signed access on the existing private S3 bucket, then a launcher with chunked delta patching -- sequenced so each tier is a strict subset of the next. Order: Tier 0 today (default *.cloudfront.net host, 24 h signed URL, publish sidecars, verify copy, watched pause-past-15-min resume test) -> Tier 1 this week (dl.ironics.org grey-cloud CNAME, logs->Athena with acct/rid attribution, mint quota via the existing rate-limit table, CloudFront Pro flat-rate $15/mo, key-rotation/kill-switch runbook, and in parallel the config-only package cull to ~3.0 GB published as 0.1.3) -> Tier 2 over the next 3-6 weeks (1-2 day BuildPatchTool spike to MEASURE the weekly delta, then the launcher -- BPS core if the spike is clean, Tauri/Rust otherwise -- with 8-16 parallel Range GETs under a 24 h signed cookie, chunk verify/repair, and per-venue pakchunks with mount-before-travel) -> Tier 3 (R2) only if sustained egress passes 50 TB/month AND R2 single-stream throughput is measured >= 100 Mbps. Decisive reasons: (1) it removes the actual root cause -- a signer bound to a credential session -- rather than the symptom; an IAM-user presigner (the only S3-direct way to a long TTL) is rejected as a throwaway that worsens secrets posture. (2) It is the repo's own plan of record (BPD s11, D1 plan s3, latest.ts:35-37 and ironics-portal-stack.ts:304-305 all say 'CloudFront + OAC layered later with no client change'); the incident is the cost of the deviation, and every hard constraint (APPROVED-only mint, immutable + provenance-gated bucket, sha256, no public URLs, AWS+Cloudflare only, unchanged client contract) survives untouched. (3) CLOUDFRONT vs R2, with numbers: today ~156 GB/month -> CloudFront $0 (free 1 TB) vs R2 ~$5 (Workers Paid) vs S3-direct ~$5; 100 testers x 4 patches (1.56 TB) -> CloudFront PAYG $48 / Pro $15 vs R2 $5 vs S3 $131; 500 x 4 (7.8 TB) -> PAYG $578 / Pro $15 vs R2 $5 vs S3 $693; 1,000 x 4 (15.6 TB) -> PAYG ~$1,213 / Pro $15 vs R2 $5 vs S3 ~$1,395; 5,000 x 4 full-zip (78 TB) -> PAYG ~$5,645 / Premium-125TB $2,250 vs R2 ~$5-10 vs S3 ~$6,260 -- BUT with Tier 2 delta patching that same 5,000-tester cohort is ~6.5 TB/month, back inside Pro's $15. So R2's only decisive win (egress at >50 TB) is exactly the regime Tier 2 is designed to prevent, while CloudFront wins today on every other axis: it edge-caches the whole 3.9 GB object (50 GB per-object cap; Cloudflare cannot cache >512 MB on Free/Pro/Business and 5 GB only on Enterprise), it needs no second copy or second publish path for a provenance-gated release, it keeps one vendor in the byte path and one authority for the gate, its signer/OAC/key-group are built in (R2 presigned URLs cannot use a custom domain and bypass WAF; a Worker gate is bespoke security code), and it is 1-2 days of pure CDK in the stack that CI already deploys. (4) 'Fairly quickly' for a 10 Mbps tester is physics: 31.25 Gbit is ~52 min on any CDN, so the real levers are (a) resumability (Tier 0), (b) fewer bytes (Tier 1B: -0.9 GB of non-game payload), and (c) not re-sending 3.3 GB of unchanged venue art every week (Tier 2 delta + per-venue chunks) -- which also collapses egress and therefore the whole cost debate. Acceptance criterion for every tier is the doctrine's: a watched download on a throttled link, paused past the old 15-minute mark, resumed, and hash-verified -- not a green build.

## Adversarial review — verdict: sound-with-fixes

The reviewer's fixes below are **part of the proposal** (each tier is to be executed with its fix applied):

- **[major] Tier 0.3 / 1A.3 — 24 h bearer signed URL with no per-link revocation** — A canned-policy CloudFront URL is a bearer token replayable without limit for 24 h by anyone who holds it; CloudFront has no per-URL download counter. The only kill switch offered (removing the public key from the key group) revokes EVERY outstanding legitimate link and takes minutes to propagate. On PAYG a single leaked link posted publicly can generate multiple TB in a day (1,000 replays x 3.9 GB = 3.9 TB = ~$330 at $0.085/GB); on Pro it burns the 50 TB allowance ('not hard limits' -> edge degradation after sustained excess, per https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/flat-rate-pricing-plan.html fetched 2026-09-06). Also the proposal itself puts `?acct=&rid=` plus `Expires/Signature/Key-Pair-Id` into `cs-uri-query`, so the Tier 1 log bucket and Athena results bucket hold LIVE bearer credentials for up to 24 h.  
  **Fix:** Add per-link revocation without key rotation: a CloudFront Function at viewer-request that 403s any `rid` present in a KeyValueStore denylist (KVS is included on Pro+; 5 MB / 512 B keys per the quotas page). Add a cost circuit breaker: CloudWatch alarm on the distribution's BytesDownloaded (e.g. > 2x expected daily) plus an AWS Budget alarm while on PAYG. Consider 12 h instead of 24 h (3.9 GB at 3 Mbps is still only ~3 h). Treat the log + Athena buckets as secret-bearing: SSE, Block Public Access, 30-day lifecycle, no cross-account access, and an Athena view that flags a `rid` fetched from >2 ASNs or >3 full-size completions for auto-denylisting.
- **[major] Tier 1A.3 — per-account mint quota (20/day) vs the existing DownloadCard mount fetch** — DownloadCard.tsx:39-55 calls GET /v1/download/latest on MOUNT (to display version/size/sha256) and again on click (line 61). latest.ts:71-78 mints a URL AND emits `download_started` on every one of those calls. So (a) a 20/day quota locks a tester out after ~10 portal page views without a single click, and (b) the funnel event the proposal plans to join telemetry against is already inflated by page views — `download_started` fires with no download.  
  **Fix:** Split the contract: a metadata-only mode (e.g. `GET /v1/download/latest?meta=1` or `/v1/download/latest/meta`) that returns {version, channel, file, sizeBytes, sha256} without minting or emitting; mint + count the quota + emit `download_started` only on the click path. Add a test that the mount path emits nothing and mints nothing. Only then set the quota (and size it for 2-3 legitimate resumes/re-clicks per patch, not 20).
- **[major] Tier 1A.4 — CloudFront Pro flat-rate plan prerequisites and constraints** — The doc (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/flat-rate-pricing-plan.html, fetched 2026-09-06) states things the proposal omits or contradicts: (1) 'You must have a AWS WAF Web ACL associated with your distribution if you're using a pricing plan' — WAF is a PREREQUISITE, not an included extra; (2) 'AWS accounts are not eligible ... [if] Your account is using AWS Free Tier' — account 302659227808 shows new-account symptoms (Lambda concurrency 10 per AWS-SETUP.md:89) so eligibility is unknown; (3) plans are managed only via console/CLI/PricingPlanManager API — a later `cdk deploy` sends a full DistributionConfig update and it is unverified whether that preserves the subscription; (4) WAF 'Rule Groups' are unsupported (individual rules only), real-time logs unsupported; (5) 'Custom caching rules', custom origin-request and custom response-header policies are Business+ ($200/mo) — Pro is managed policies only; (6) Pro allows 10 cache behaviors, 25 WAF rules; (7) 'Each pricing plan covers one CloudFront distribution'.  
  **Fix:** Re-sequence Tier 1: WAF web ACL (CDK `webAclId`) deploys BEFORE the plan subscription; confirm the account is not on Free Tier before promising $15/mo; subscribe out-of-band, then run one more `cdk deploy` and re-read the subscription via `PricingPlanManager` to prove CloudFormation does not strip it (document the result in AWS-SETUP.md); keep every behavior on managed policies (CachingOptimized + managed origin-request/response-header policies) so the design never silently requires Business; write the WAF rate rule as an individual rule, not a rule group.
- **[major] Tier 1B(iii) — 'UltimateDifficultyScaling drags 221 MB of CEF3'** — Wrong attribution, verified on disk: UDS's WebBrowserWidget plugin dependency is already `TargetAllowList: ["Editor"]` and its only `WebBrowser` module dependency is on the EDITOR module (Plugins/UltimateDifficultyScaling/UltimateDifficultyScaling.uplugin:26-46). The 211 MB `D:\BagMan\StagedBuilds\Windows\Engine\Binaries\ThirdParty\CEF3` + `Engine/Binaries/Win64/EpicWebHelper.exe` are staged because `OnlineFramework` (enabled at Bag_Man.uproject:190) ships the `LoginFlow` module (Type ClientOnly, OnlineFramework.uplugin:43-47) which links `WebBrowser` (LoginFlow.Build.cs:26), and WebBrowser.Build.cs:72-91 adds CEF3/EpicWebHelper as RuntimeDependencies. Making UDS editor-only would ship zero savings.  
  **Fix:** Set `bCompileCEF3 = false` in the client Target.cs (UBT TargetRules.cs:1032-1033; config-driven via `[/Script/BuildSettings.BuildSettings] bCompileCEF3`) so WebBrowser builds without CEF and stages nothing — or exclude LoginFlow. First confirm no in-game web login is used (EOS account-portal flow is external browser in this project). Prove by staged-dir diff (`Engine/Binaries/ThirdParty/CEF3` absent, exe still links).
- **[major] Tier 1B(i) — `TargetAllowList: ["Editor"]` on AgentIntegrationKit to drop MetaHuman content from the cook** — AIK's modules are ALL `EditorNoCommandlet` already (AgentIntegrationKit.uplugin, 25 module entries), so module scoping changes nothing; the payload is the optional plugin deps' CONTENT/ini. The cook runs inside the Editor target, where a plugin allow-listed for Editor stays enabled, and the cooker's plugin-content filter (D:\UE5.6-source\Engine\Source\Editor\UnrealEd\Private\CookOnTheFlyServer.cpp:10865-10880) only excludes plugins by `SupportedTargetPlatforms` — it never consults TargetAllowList. So the mechanism as written is unlikely to remove the bytes. The 323 MB figure is also unverified by me (pak index is encrypted, Config/DefaultCrypto.ini:4 `bEncryptPakIndex=True`).  
  **Fix:** Use levers the cooker honours: explicit `{"Name":"MetaHumanCharacter","Enabled":false}` / `MetaHumanSDK` entries in Bag_Man.uproject (legal because AIK declares them `Optional: true`, AgentIntegrationKit.uplugin:431-439) and/or `DirectoriesToNeverCook` for `/MetaHumanCharacter`, `/MetaHumanSDK`, `/NNEDenoiser`; then prove with the cook manifest diff + cooked boot, per the proposal's own doctrine. Same for NNEDenoiser: it is not in the uproject at all (engine EnabledByDefault), so it needs an explicit disable entry.
- **[minor] Tier 0.4 — `aws s3 cp --checksum-algorithm SHA256` as an integrity feature** — A 3.9 GB `aws s3 cp` is a multipart upload; S3 stores a COMPOSITE (checksum-of-part-checksums) for SHA-256 — 'Full object checksums in multipart uploads are only available for CRC-based checksums' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity-upload.html, fetched 2026-09-06). It cannot be compared to the sidecar whole-file sha256 and does not validate what the tester downloads.  
  **Fix:** Drop the flag (default CRC64NVME full-object is fine) or keep it only as transport integrity; the publish gate is `head-object ContentLength == local size` plus the local sha256 written to latest.json/manifest.json/.sha256 sidecar; optionally re-hash by downloading through CloudFront once in the acceptance step.
- **[major] Tier 2A/2B — BuildPatchServices delta size estimate and request economics** — BPS matches FIXED 1 MiB chunks by exact content (BuildPatchSettings.cpp:171 `OutputChunkSize(1024*1024)`). pakchunk0-Windows.ucas (3,529,187,744 B) is Oodle-compressed 64 KB blocks; if cook order shifts between builds the blocks reorder and no 1 MiB window matches an old chunk, so a 'weekly patch' can approach the full container — the 100-500 MB figure has no measurement behind it. Second, a fresh install via 1 MiB chunk files is ~3,725 GETs; 1,000 testers x 4 installs = 14.9M requests/month, above Pro's 10M request allowance, and a naive WAF IP rate-based rule (min 10, windows 60-600 s, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-high-level-settings.html) will block a legitimate launcher doing 8-16 parallel chunk GETs (~360-3,000 req/min).  
  **Fix:** Make the 2A spike two-armed: (a) BPS PatchGeneration/DiffManifest on 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 (both zips exist: 3,928,491,536 and 3,906,129,510 B) AND on a same-content re-cook, to separate content churn from ordering churn; (b) UE-native `-basedonreleaseversion/-generatepatch` (`_P` container, package-granular, engine-canonical: https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/how-to-create-a-patch-in-unreal-engine) — often the cheaper weekly-patch path and no launcher needed for the patch itself. Stabilize cook order (order file) before trusting any delta. Use BPS `PackageChunks` (.chunkdb) for fresh installs so a full install is a handful of large Range GETs, and scope WAF rate rules per cache behavior with thresholds far above launcher rates (e.g. 20,000/5 min on the chunk path).
- **[major] Tier 2C — per-venue pak chunks and the matchmaking join path** — The gate proposed is only the hub door (`AFLHubTravelComponent.cpp:48 ServerTravel`). In the live flow a GameLift placement (S12 dedicated server) can seat a client on a venue whose pakchunk is not mounted; with `bShouldAcquireMissingChunksOnLoad=False` (DefaultGame.ini:106) that client fails map load and drops. Any precondition in the match-accept/join path touches the surface the BPD v2 addendum declares MOST protected (playlists, experiences, AFLOnline, allocator/join). Authoring trap on top: PrimaryAssetLabel scanning is configured only for `/Game` (DefaultGame.ini:95), while Lyra's chunk assignment lives in GameFeatureData rules (AFLHub.uasset and ShooterCore.uasset both contain `ChunkId`, neither contains `PrimaryAssetLabel`); World Partition cell chunk inheritance is unverified.  
  **Fix:** Rule first, build second: either keep every matchmaking venue in the base package (chunk only hub/cosmetics/optional content, which still removes ~0.8 GB) or get an explicit operator ruling that the client's match-accept path may gain a 'required chunks mounted' precondition (with bot/queue never travelling to an unmounted map). Author chunk rules inside each GameFeatureData's PrimaryAssetTypesToScan (or extend the label scan dirs to each plugin mount), and verify WP cells land in the venue chunk via the cook chunk manifest before any UI work.
- **[minor] root_cause_of_incident — 'raising URL_TTL_SECONDS is silently capped at roughly one hour'** — AWS states the URL dies with the role session and that STS AssumeRole defaults to 1 h (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-presigned-url.html, fetched 2026-09-06), but the actual lifetime of a Lambda execution environment's credentials is not documented there; stating 'would have failed this same tester' is plausible, not verified. The conclusion (session-bound signer is the wrong tool) stands.  
  **Fix:** Word it as 'bounded by the Lambda credential lifetime (undocumented, at most the role's max session)'; keep the CloudFront key-group signer as the fix — it is credential-independent, which is the actual property needed.
- **[minor] Tier 0.4/0.5 — Content-Disposition / Cache-Control on already-published objects** — The headers only apply to NEW uploads; the live 0.1.2 object has none. A CloudFront custom response-headers policy would add them, but that is Business+ on flat-rate plans, and 'Signed-URL + CopyObject' is not mentioned.  
  **Fix:** For already-published versions do a single `CopyObject` with MetadataDirective=REPLACE (3.9 GB < 5 GB single-copy limit; creates a new version of the same key with identical bytes and sha256 — immutability preserved) or accept the URL-derived filename; add the headers to publish-release.ps1 for everything going forward.
- **[minor] Tier 2B — 'Tier 1's custom domain is mandatory for Tier 2 signed cookies' and launcher sign-in** — Overstated: a native launcher can send `CloudFront-Policy/Signature/Key-Pair-Id` (or a signed URL rewrite) per chunk through `FChunkUriResponse.AdditionalHeaders` (BuildPatchMessage.h:73, applied at DownloadService.cpp:218-221) on the default *.cloudfront.net host; the custom domain only matters for browser-cookie delivery. Meanwhile the launcher's own sign-in (magic link / Epic OAuth from a native app) is unscoped — the API already accepts a bearer token (`readSessionToken`, apps/api/src/lib/http.ts:53-55), but obtaining it from a desktop app is not designed.  
  **Fix:** State the dependency correctly (custom domain = branding + browser cookies, not a launcher blocker) and add a launcher auth item: system-browser login that hands the JWT back via a localhost loopback or device-code style exchange, reusing the bearer path.
- **[minor] Tier 0.3 tests — download.test.ts / grants.test.ts edits** — download.test.ts:60-75 presigns locally with dummy static creds; a CloudFront signer needs an RSA private key and a Secrets Manager read, neither of which the fake S3 client provides, so the handler must take the signing material via `ctx`/injection or the tests will hit AWS. grants.test.ts is DynamoDB-only (line 82 comment), so the narrowed `win64/latest.json` S3 grant is not asserted anywhere.  
  **Fix:** Inject the signer (keyPairId + PEM) through `Ctx` with a test RSA keypair generated in-test; add a synth-level assertion (cdk assertions) that DownloadLatestFn's S3 statement is scoped to `win64/latest.json` and the new secret ARN.

**Missing from the first draft (now folded in above):**

- Per-link revocation and cost circuit breakers: CloudFront Function + KeyValueStore `rid` denylist (Pro+), CloudWatch BytesDownloaded alarm, AWS Budgets alarm while on PAYG, and an Athena 'replayed rid' detector — today the only lever is a key-group removal that kills all legitimate downloads.
- Metadata-only endpoint so the DownloadCard mount fetch stops minting URLs and emitting `download_started` (DownloadCard.tsx:43 -> latest.ts:71-78) — required before any mint quota and to make the funnel honest.
- Flat-rate plan prerequisites: WAF web ACL must exist BEFORE subscribing; account must not be on AWS Free Tier; plan is console/CLI/PricingPlanManager-only — prove a subsequent `cdk deploy` keeps the subscription; WAF rule groups unsupported; custom cache/origin-request/response-header policies are Business+ ($200) so Pro means managed policies only (10 behaviors, 25 rules).
- UE-native patching path not evaluated: `-CreateReleaseVersion` / `-BasedOnReleaseVersion -GeneratePatch` `_P` containers are package-granular, engine-canonical, and need no launcher for the weekly-patch case; the 2A spike should measure it beside BPS, plus stabilize cook order before trusting any delta number.
- BPS request economics: 1 MiB chunk files -> ~3,725 GETs per fresh 3.9 GB install (14.9M requests/month at 1,000 testers x 4, above Pro's 10M allowance); use `PackageChunks` (.chunkdb) for fresh installs and scope WAF rate rules per behavior so a launcher's 8-16 parallel streams are not blocked.
- CEF3 root cause is `OnlineFramework/LoginFlow` (ClientOnly, links WebBrowser), not UltimateDifficultyScaling; the real lever is `bCompileCEF3=false` in the client Target.cs — 211 MB + EpicWebHelper.exe verified in the staged build.
- UE cook gotcha: `TargetAllowList: ["Editor"]` on a uproject plugin does not remove that plugin's (or its optional deps') content from the cook — the cooker filters plugin content by platform only (CookOnTheFlyServer.cpp:10865-10880); explicit `Enabled:false` on the optional MetaHuman deps and/or `DirectoriesToNeverCook`, proven by manifest diff, is the mechanism. NNEDenoiser is engine-enabled-by-default and needs an explicit disable entry.
- Matchmaking/join-path precondition for per-venue chunks (GameLift placement onto an unmounted venue) — touches the BPD-protected allocator/join surface and needs its own operator ruling; hub-door gating alone is insufficient. Plus: PrimaryAssetLabel scan dirs are `/Game`-only (DefaultGame.ini:95) while Lyra chunk rules live in GameFeatureData assets; WP cell chunk inheritance unverified.
- Log hygiene: CloudFront `cs-uri-query` will contain live `Signature/Key-Pair-Id/Expires` for 24 h — the log bucket and Athena results bucket must be treated as credential stores (SSE, Block Public Access, tight IAM, short lifecycle).
- S3 checksum trap: multipart SHA-256 is composite, not the whole-file hash; the sidecar sha256 + ContentLength assert is the real gate.
- Migration trap for already-published objects: no Content-Disposition/Cache-Control on 0.1.2; fix via single CopyObject (metadata replace, <5 GB) which preserves bytes/sha256 and immutability.
- Tier 0 acceptance should include the SHIPPING path (Chrome and Edge `window.location.href` download, pause > 15 min, browser restart, Resume -> 206) not only `curl -C -`; ETag pass-through from S3 via CloudFront is what browser resume keys on.
